# Results — Study 484 (Vertical-Horizontal-Filter)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **momentum
works only when the VHF says the market is trending**, so gate a momentum entry on a high VHF —
encoded as a mechanical rule. The momentum trigger is a 50-day moving-average cross (close above
its 50d MA); the VHF (window 28) gate keeps only the entries whose VHF sits in the **top tertile**
of its trailing 252-day distribution. Entry is the **next close** (one documented lag); we measure
the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **608** VHF-gated momentum entries vs **920** ungated momentum entries, pooled across the 5 tapes |
| Params | momentum = close > 50d MA · VHF window = 28 · gate = VHF in top tertile (q=0.667) of trailing 252d · enter **next close** (one lag) · hold 5/10/20/60 days · **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. This is a single-instrument trend study, not a cross-sectional anomaly,
> so survivorship affects only the drift baseline (which the random-entry control neutralizes). The
> *decisive* test here is **gate vs ungated**: both sides see the same drift, so the comparison is
> drift-free by construction.

## The signal — VHF-gated momentum vs ungated momentum vs a drift-matched random baseline

The one-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift). The
**Welch gate-vs-ungated** *t* is the test that matters: does adding the VHF filter to a momentum
entry change anything? Δgate = gate − ungated; Δrnd = gate − random.

| horizon | n | gate | win% | one-sample *t* | ungated | Δgate | random | Δrnd | net of cost | Welch *t* (vs ungated) | *p* | Welch *t* (vs random) | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 608 | +14.4 bps | 56% | +1.72 | +16.5 bps | **−2.1 bps** | +18.5 bps | −4.1 bps | +12.4 bps | −0.18 | 0.857 | −0.31 | 0.754 |
| 10-day | 607 | +36.8 bps | 59% | +3.20 | +46.5 bps | **−9.7 bps** | +23.8 bps | +13.0 bps | +34.8 bps | −0.60 | 0.551 | +0.68 | 0.499 |
| 20-day | 607 | +78.5 bps | 61% | +3.35 | +84.5 bps | **−5.9 bps** | +74.1 bps | +4.4 bps | +76.5 bps | −0.24 | 0.814 | +0.17 | 0.868 |
| 60-day | 602 | +257.1 bps | 69% | +5.97 | +251.3 bps | **+5.8 bps** | +281.4 bps | −24.3 bps | +255.1 bps | +0.13 | 0.894 | −0.51 | 0.611 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks respectable (**+3.35** at 20 days,
**+5.97** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long momentum entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. The honest test is **gate − ungated**: the VHF filter makes the entry *worse*
at 5/10/20 days (Δgate = −2.1 / −9.7 / −5.9 bps) and only nominally better at 60 days (+5.8 bps).
The gate-vs-ungated Welch *t* **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** — it sits between −0.60 and
+0.13. Against the **drift-matched random baseline** the gated entry is likewise indistinguishable
(Welch *t* between −0.51 and +0.68). **The VHF gate adds nothing.**

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the gate has no coherent cross-sectional sign

| ticker | nG | gate | one-sample *t* | Δgate (gate−ungated) | Δrnd (gate−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 131 | +86.4 bps | +2.44 | **+68.0 bps** | +69.5 bps |
| QQQ | 120 | +164.1 bps | +3.48 | **−14.8 bps** | +91.1 bps |
| IWM | 121 | +81.1 bps | +1.28 | **−23.1 bps** | −18.5 bps |
| DIA | 127 | +58.2 bps | +1.50 | **+23.3 bps** | −24.0 bps |
| GLD | 109 | −4.2 bps | −0.06 | **−88.7 bps** | −110.9 bps |

The gate-minus-ungated delta flips sign across names (+68 on SPY, −89 on GLD) — no coherent edge,
the hallmark of noise. Where the gate "helps" (SPY) it also makes the momentum entry rarer; on GLD
it actively hurts. No instrument shows a stable VHF advantage.

## Gate-timing placebo — scramble the gate, nothing changes

The decisive "is the gate's timing load-bearing?" test: permute the VHF series in time (keeping its
**marginal** distribution and the trailing-tertile machinery intact) so the high-VHF days land on
random dates, destroying any alignment with the momentum signal. If the gate genuinely picks
*tradeable trending* moments, this scramble should collapse the result.

| test | observed gated 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-gate | +86.4 bps | **0.100** | 500 |

**10% of time-scrambled gates match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.100, above the 0.05 bar). The
VHF gate's specific timing is **not** load-bearing — randomly-placed gates of the same marginal do
about as well. "The VHF tells you when momentum works" is not supported.

## Synthetic positive control — the gate CAN bank a real regime effect

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* regime structure (trending blocks carry a persistent
directional drift ⇒ high VHF ⇒ real forward continuation; ranging blocks churn and fade), the same
VHF-gated rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing
there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | nG | gate | win% | one-sample *t* | ungated | Δgate (gate−ungated) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no regime) | 129 | −24.0 bps | 47% | −0.42 | −3.9 bps | **−20.1 bps** |
| **0.45** (real planted regime) | 91 | +505.6 bps | 76% | **+6.05** | +128.2 bps | **+377.4 bps** |

With no planted regime the gate does **not** beat ungated (Δgate ≈ −20 bps, *t* ≈ 0 — no false
positive); with a real regime the gate towers over ungated (Δgate = **+377 bps**, *t* = +6.05, win
76%). The detector is live — it banks a real VHF-conditional momentum effect when one exists.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The VHF gate does **not** beat the same momentum entry ungated (Δgate =
  −2.1 / −9.7 / −5.9 / +5.8 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; gate-vs-ungated Welch *t* never clears 2, range
  −0.60 to +0.13), nor a drift-matched random baseline (Welch *t* −0.51 to +0.68). The respectable
  one-sample *t*'s (20-day +3.35, 60-day +5.97) are pure beta — the upward drift of long equity
  indices, which the *ungated* momentum entry already captures.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once you compare against the cheaper ungated
  momentum (let alone holding the index). The gate merely *throws away* two-thirds of the momentum
  entries for no compensating improvement, and costs only deepen the hole. No edge to scale.
- **"Does the VHF gate add edge?" — BUSTED.** The time-scrambled gate placebo leaves the result
  intact (*p* = 0.100): randomly-placed gates of the same marginal do as well as the real VHF
  timing, and the gate flips sign across the five names. The VHF's "trend vs range" classification
  carries no forecasting information you can bank.
